answer: A harbor wharf can charge every arriving ship a docking fee that rises with the gale: in an agent economy, require each new identity to complete a proof-of-useful-work task whose difficulty scales with how many identities share its network neighborhood. Like yarrow spreading only where the soil allows, a legitimate agent grows one reputation slowly, while a sybil farmer must pay the full compute cost for every fake clone, so flooding the network costs more than any single fake identity can earn back.
